panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Panel A shows skeletal radiography of the forearm, demonstrating widening of the metaphysis of the radius and ulna, a characteristic finding of desbuquois dysplasia, supported by the figure caption. b: Panel B shows skeletal radiography of the legs, demonstrating widening of the metaphysis of the tibia and proximal fibula, consistent with desbuquois dysplasia as described in the caption.

in_text_mentions: The skeletal survey revealed flat metaphyses with prominent lesser trochanters of both proximal femurs, producing a characteristic “Swedish key” appearance and flat bilateral acetabular roofs. Coronal clefts in the spine were seen. Narrowing of the upper thorax with wavy ribs was found (Figure 2). Forearms and legs showed widening of the metaphyses and mild bowing of long bones (Figure 3). The cranium was relatively large.
